messages:
oncall-bot: ALERT: increased pod evictions in namespace=redwood-inference-pool-1 -> 18 pods NotReady/CrashLoopBackOff since 16:07 UTC :rotating_light:

Anika Patel: seeing the same in grafana. Node health shows a bunch of NotReady spikes across us-west-2-c cluster. impact: inference pool serving latency +5-10x for a small subset of customers. paging @SRE Rotation

Jonas Meyer: paging in. initial hypothesis: kubelet OOMs + docker/containerd restarts. kubelet logs show repeated "failed to start heartbeat" around 16:05 and then node status flip to NotReady.

Priya Sharma: confirmed. `kubectl get nodes` shows 4 nodes in NotReady in the inference pool nodegroup (ig-ml-infer-*-usw2). Node events: `kubelet: runtime network not ready` then `kubelet: evicting pods` followed by container runtime restarts.

Ethan Wong: I can take lead on mitigation. Action plan: 1) cordon the affected nodes 2) increase inference-pool replica-set to absorb traffic 3) trigger routed canary fallback to lower-memory model variants for impacted customers 4) capture kubelet+docker logs and kernel OOM traces.

Anika Patel: sounds good. I'm going to open a quick customer-impact note in #incidents and flag the customers currently routed through this pool (we have a short list, approx 6 customers).

Priya Sharma: adding immediate commands:
```
kubectl cordon ig-ml-infer-045
kubectl drain ig-ml-infer-045 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
kubectl scale deploy/redwood-infer-pool --replicas=30 -n redwood-inference
```
I'll run these but want someone to watch autoscaler to ensure we don't cause more churn.

Jonas Meyer: I'm watching ASG and the cluster-autoscaler. ASG currently has capacity to spin 6 more nodes, starting now. Also increasing pod disruption budgets to allow safe drains.

oncall-bot: NOTE: oncall handoff in 1h to SRE Rotation. Incident priority P2.

Ethan Wong: executing drains now. Also enabling routing fallback: update routing policy for pool-1 to send 30% traffic to pool-2 (healthy) and 20% to dedicated-fallback (cheaper, lower-memory model). Using admin route: `PATCH /routing/policies/pool-1` with body `{ "fallback": ["pool-2", "dedicated-fallback"], "weights": [0.3,0.2] }`. cc @Anika

Anika Patel: customer-impact note: customers A23, BetaMetrics, and RetailX show elevated latency and a few 5xx spikes. I'm pinging their CSMs and will post a short update in the customer-facing status page: "We are investigating degraded inference performance in us-west-2; mitigation in progress."

Priya Sharma: logs pulled from one problematic node:
```
[16:04:56] kubelet[pid=2103]: runtime-cgroup: container runtime restart detected
[16:05:02] kernel: oom_kill_process: Killed process 31245 (nn-server) total-vm: 1624872kB, anon-rss: 1380744kB
[16:05:03] kubelet: eviction manager: pods evicted due to memoryPressure
```
So this is consistent with OOMs on nodes running large-model containers.

Jonas Meyer: to reduce memory pressure, I'm lowering max model batch size via runtime config for pool-1 and forcing quantized model variants where available: runtime flag `--max-batch=8 --quantize=fp16` to free RAM. Applying to all replicas in pool-2 as well to keep capacity.

Ethan Wong: verbose: I restarted kubelet on ig-ml-infer-045 after collecting logs (journalctl saved at /tmp/ig-045-kubelet.log). Node came back NotReady -> Ready after ~75s, but some pods are CrashLoopBackOff due to previous OOMs. I'm re-creating the pods with pinned lower-memory model.

Anika Patel: monitoring customer error budgets after routing change. early telemetry: tail latency reduced ~40% for BetaMetrics after routing fallback. still some 5xx from the few pods that crashed.

oncall-bot: ACTION: create incident ticket INC-2026-1182 and assign to SRE Rotation.

Priya Sharma: we should also capture kernel vmstat and `dmesg` from affected nodes to check for swap pressure or memory fragmentation. I'm collecting those and uploading to the incident ticket.

Jonas Meyer: discovered a pattern: nodes provisioned with kernel image v5.15.2 show higher OOM rate with our runtime. Newer nodes with v5.16.9 are stable. Suggest rolling the nodegroup image or applying the kernel patch to affected nodes.

Ethan Wong: short-term mitigation complete: cordoned/drained 4 nodes, scaled pool to 30 replicas, routing fallback active, lowered batch/quantization configs applied. Still seeing 5 crashed pods being recreated; re-scheduling them onto healthy nodes.

Anika Patel: customer comms: posted update to status page and emailed CSMs for A23 and RetailX with current mitigations and ETA for full recovery (T+45m).

Priya Sharma: collecting post-incident artifacts: kubelet logs, containerd logs, dmesg, core dumps for crashed inference containers, and runtime metrics. Planning a root-cause triage: kernel OOM interaction with our memory alloc patterns in the serving runtime + model size foot-printing.

Jonas Meyer: long-term work items I've added to backlog: 1) node AMI upgrade to kernel v5.16+ for inference nodegroups 2) add OOM-score adjustment and early eviction for large-model pods 3) smarter routing: pre-emptive fallbacks when node churn > X/min 4) autoscaler tuning to prefer warm spare nodes.

Ethan Wong: handing incident to next oncall (SRE Rotation) in 35m. I'll attach collected logs to INC-2026-1182.

oncall-bot: RESOLVE: some metrics returned to baseline after 00:38:00 of mitigation steps. Recommend postmortem and RCA.

Anika Patel: creating postmortem draft, will include timeline, customer impact, mitigations, and action items from Jonas and Priya.

SRE Rotation: acknowledged handoff. I'll continue follow-up, owner for INC-2026-1182. Please drop any remaining artifacts in the ticket.

Jonas Meyer: final note: if we see this pattern again, priority one is to flip routing fallback early and avoid large-batch scheduling until nodes are confirmed stable.

Anika Patel: thanks team. tagging for postmortem: @Priya, @Jonas, @Ethan.

(End of thread)
